Differential Associations

Source: R/assoc_network_diff.r
assoc_network_diff.Rd

Tests, for every pair of features, whether their correlation differs between two groups of samples, with Fisher's \(z\) test, as NetCoMi's diffnet(diffMethod = "fisherTest") does.

Usage

assoc_network_diff(x, y, alpha = 0.05, p_adjust = "BH", n_samples = NULL)

Arguments

x, y

The two groups' correlations between the same features: two results of the same method, one whose values are Pearson-type correlations (today, sparcc()), or two symmetric matrices of Pearson correlations with 1 on the diagonal (with n_samples). Features are matched by name.

alpha

The adjusted p-value at most which a difference is called significant (the reject column). Default 0.05.

p_adjust

How to adjust the p-values for testing every pair: one of stats::p.adjust.methods. Default 'BH'.

n_samples

The numbers of samples that x and y were estimated from: one number for both, or two. Needed for matrices; NULL (the default) takes them from the results' n_samples attributes.

Value

A data frame of class c("ecodive_network_diff", "data.frame"), one row per pair of features, with columns:

  • feature1, feature2: the pair, feature1 first in x's input table.

  • association_x, association_y: their correlation in each group.

  • z: Fisher's \(z\) statistic.

  • p_value, p_adjusted: its two-sided p-value, and that adjusted by p_adjust over all pairs.

  • reject: whether p_adjusted is at most alpha.

Attributes: method (the method that made x and y, when they are results), alpha, p_adjust, and display (the title; see ecodive_display). plot() draws the pairs with reject as a network (plot.ecodive_network_diff()).

Details

Each correlation is transformed with Fisher's \(z = \mathrm{atanh}(r)\), and the difference is divided by its standard error:

$$z = \frac{\mathrm{atanh}\,r_x - \mathrm{atanh}\,r_y}{\sqrt{1/(n_x - 3) + 1/(n_y - 3)}}$$

which is standard normal when the two population correlations are equal. Pairs with \(|r| \ge 1\) in either group, or a missing correlation, get NA (with a warning for \(|r| \ge 1\)).

For sparcc() this is an approximation: its correlations are medians over Dirichlet draws of an estimate, not sample Pearson correlations, so their sampling variance isn't exactly \(1/(n - 3)\). rho_p() isn't accepted (a concordance, not a correlation); neither are partial correlations, whose test needs other degrees of freedom.

Names in NetCoMi. p_adjust is adjust; alpha is alpha. NetCoMi's default adjustment is the local false discovery rate; here only stats::p.adjust()'s methods are offered. NetCoMi's resampling-based tests ("permute", "discordant") aren't offered.

See also

assoc_network(), assoc_network_compare(), sparcc().

Examples

    # Two groups of 60 samples; taxa 1 and 2 correlated only in the first
    set.seed(1)
    make <- function (linked) {
      basis <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 10), 60, 10)
      if (linked) basis[, 2] <- basis[, 1] + rnorm(60, sd = 0.3)
      matrix(rpois(600, exp(basis + 4)), 60, 10,
             dimnames = list(NULL, paste0('OTU', 1:10)))
    }
    rx <- sparcc(make(TRUE),  n_draws = 20)
    ry <- sparcc(make(FALSE), n_draws = 20)

    d <- assoc_network_diff(rx, ry)
    d
